record.what_it_does: Gorgias is an ecommerce-focused helpdesk platform that unifies customer support channels (email, chat, social, SMS, voice) into one inbox with automation and an AI agent.
record.auth_notes: Private apps (single-account use) authenticate via HTTP Basic auth using the account email as username and an API key as password. Public apps (App Store listings, multi-customer) must use OAuth2 with an authorization-code flow against https://{subdomain}.gorgias.com/oauth/authorize and /oauth/token.
record.access_notes: Any developer can sign up for a 7-day free trial (no credit card) and immediately generate a private-app API key from their own account. There is no permanent free plan, so ongoing/production use requires a paid Gorgias subscription. Building a public OAuth2 app additionally requires registering on the Developer Portal, obtaining a Sandbox account from techpartners@gorgias.com, and passing Gorgias's app review before publishing to the App Store.
record.main_blocker: Public/multi-user OAuth2 apps require Gorgias Developer Portal registration, a sandbox grant, and app-store review before production use; self-serve access otherwise requires an ongoing paid Gorgias plan (no permanent free tier).

evidence.quote: The Gorgias API supports two authentication methods: 1. 🔐 Private app → API key 2. 👥 Public app → OAuth2
The username will be the email address of your Gorgias account and the password will be your API key.
You don't need to follow any special process to create a private app...you can use Access Tokens.
7-day trial | All features unlocked | No credit card required
Get Gorgias Sandbox to test your app: create a trial account and reach out to techpartners@gorgias.com to convert it into a Sandbox account.
The Gorgias API is structured with REST in mind. Our API has predictable resource-oriented URLs
In the Remote MCP server URL field, enter the following URL: https://mcp.gorgias.com/mcp

record.open_questions: Whether the per-endpoint OpenAPI 3.1 definitions embedded in developers.gorgias.com are offered as a single downloadable spec file (e.g. a combined openapi.json) was not directly confirmed, though each reference page is generated from a vendor-authored OpenAPI 3.1 document.
